answer: In an agent marketplace for terrace plans, umber pigments, and mesa surveys, each seller identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving one active job slot. The bond stays locked even if the identity quits, so an attacker cannot recycle the same money through fresh accounts. Running 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up $100,000 for a month: identities remain cheap to invent, but capacity to crowd out honest agents scales with committed capital.
